active_hypotheses: Pure time-skip for the DSP2 CVR poll loop is unsafe: CVR reads must still invoke m_readCvrCallback so DSP catch-up and host-command acceptance timing remain real.

A full CVR loop accelerator is only viable if it batches taken iterations while still performing CVR reads and checking host-pump/deferred-RX/IRQ/timer/MIDI boundaries between MOVE and BLT. The single-MOVE fast path is rejected by measurement.

DSP2 heavier steady-state wall time is real work, but the large per-block spikes are now attributed to synchronous live DSP JIT compilation inside render callbacks; steady non-JIT windows still hover near the 5.805 ms budget and need separate DSP2 throughput work.

A simple first-PC/static-branch prewarm is insufficient: the trace shows many dynamic/low-vector repeated compile events after boot. Next evidence target is why already-seen PCs recompile (mode chain proliferation vs P-memory invalidation vs dynamic dispatch entrypoints).
next_steps: If continuing UC work, prototype a full taken-iteration CVR loop batch with explicit post-CVR host boundary checks, not the rejected single-MOVE path.

If continuing DSP work, first instrument JIT creation reasons/modes and P-memory invalidations around repeated PCs (000235/000208/00000c/000010/000012/000014) before another prewarm/deferred-compile prototype. A prewarm that cannot explain repeats is likely a false fix.
After JIT spikes are removed, target steady DSP2 throughput because dsp2 remains the largest total wall-time component (~149.55 ms/window vs uc ~113.18 ms and dsp1 ~98.34 ms in v21 profile).
Run host/VST3 smoke with Thor after any default-on perf change; headless probes alone are not host acceptance.
